nodes.title: START HERE
widgets_values:
# Load PSD — start a workflow from a layered file

**Load PSD** reads a `.psd`, `.psb`, `.tif` or `.tiff` out of `ComfyUI/input/`,
flattens it, and hands it to the rest of the graph. No Photoshop needed just to
load a file — this half runs anywhere.

**The `psd` dropdown is empty until there's a file to pick.** Three ways to
fill it:

- Click **Upload Photoshop File** on the node and choose one.
- Drag a `.psd` straight onto the node.
- Drop a file into `ComfyUI/input/` yourself, then reload the page.

No PSD handy? Queue the **`compose-layers-to-psd.json`** demo once — it needs
no Photoshop and writes `compose_00001.psd` into exactly the right folder. It
will be in this dropdown the next time you look.

The node ships with `psd` deliberately blank, because whatever we typed in here
wouldn't exist on your machine. Pick your file, then queue.

nodes.title: edit_original and on_save
widgets_values:
# Sending it back to Photoshop

Right-click the node and choose **Open in Photoshop** to push the file back for
editing. With the panel plugin connected that's instant; without it, the node
opens the file and watches for your save. Either way works.

**`edit_original`** — off (the default) means your original file is **never
touched**: your edit is saved to a working copy alongside it. Turn it on to
edit the file in place. Leave it off unless you really mean it.

**`on_save`** — what happens the moment you save in Photoshop:

- **Re-run workflow** — the whole workflow queues again with your edit. Good
  for "tweak, look, tweak again."
- **Update only (don't re-run)** — the node quietly picks up the new version;
  nothing runs until you queue it yourself.
- **Ignore (do nothing)** — saves are ignored entirely.

**The lower branch** turns the MASK output into something you can actually look
at. It marks transparency in the file: white where the flattened image has
nothing in it, black where it has pixels. A PSD with a full background layer
gives you an all-black mask — that's right, not broken.
